capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Toyota says only "full capacity of 41.8 kWh" in Extended Mode (Standard Mode 35 kWh); Toyota does not label it gross.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Green Car Reports: "41.8 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity"; Wikipedia: 41.8 kWh usable. Standard Mode (default) charges to 35 kWh per Toyota, so the everyday usable figure is lower.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia (RAV4 EV): pack, electronics and powertrain "similar to" the Tesla Model S, about 4,500 Panasonic cells; Wikipedia (Model S): 18650 cells with a nickel-cobalt-aluminum cathode. Inference only: a Tesla-designed pack with Model S-type cells; neither Toyota nor Wikipedia names the RAV4 EV cell chemistry.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: The Toyota 2012 pressroom page describes charging (240 V/40 A, about six hours) with a liquid-cooled pack and no battery-warming or preconditioning feature; the car has no DC charging, so DC preconditioning does not apply.

ac_max_kw.notes: Green Car Reports: the Tesla-designed charger "can charge at up to 10 kilowatts" (Wikipedia: 9.6 kW / 10 kW).

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia: only a J1772 240 V 40 A input; DC quick charge appears only as a third-party aftermarket upgrade (Quick Charge Power, 48 kW CHAdeMO); neither Toyota nor Green Car Reports mentions DC charging. Same car 2012-2014.
